close_reason: Closed in single doc pass commit. The new '# Contract guarantees' (or '# Features') section in pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs covers this finding.
description:
pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs nowhere documents what from_pem / from_der_iter
do when the input contains the same certificate twice (or more). The impl
preserves duplicates: the returned Vec<TrustAnchor> has N entries for N
copies in the input, and no equality dedup is performed.

What goes wrong for a caller in production:

  - Real-world bundles ship with the same root multiple times. Debian's
    update-ca-certificates can include the same CA from multiple source
    packages (e.g., 'mozilla-ca' + a vendor-specific package). A caller
    loading such a bundle gets N anchors for the same SPKI+Subject,
    consuming memory and slowing path validation (every anchor is a
    candidate in chain_walk's anchor-matching loop).
  - A caller intersecting two trust stores ('my custom roots' UNION 'OS
    bundle') has no contract telling them whether intersection by content
    is necessary or whether the crate handles it.
  - Diagnostic tools reporting 'you trust 147 roots' vs 'you trust 145
    distinct roots' get different answers depending on whether the tool
    dedups.

Fix options:

  a) Document the current behavior:
       /// Duplicate certificates in the input are preserved as duplicate
       /// `TrustAnchor` values. Callers needing deduplication should filter
       /// the returned `Vec` on their preferred equality (typically
       /// `subject_public_key_info`).

  b) Add a dedup pass keyed off SPKI bytes before returning. This is what
     most real callers want. Performance is fine — anchor loads happen once
     at startup, and dedup on a HashSet<&[u8]> over the SPKI bytes is O(N).

  c) Add a `from_pem_dedup` variant. The default stays 'preserve', the
     opt-in variant filters.

Option (a) is the minimal fix; (b) makes the API do the right thing by
default; (c) is the conservative middle ground. Pre-1.0 the maintainer can
pick (b) cheaply; post-1.0 it is a breaking semantic change.

Note: TrustAnchor derives PartialEq (per pkix-path/src/lib.rs:648), so
content-equality dedup is straightforward for either crate-side or
caller-side filtering. The contract gap is documentation, regardless of
which option is chosen.
title: Duplicate-cert behavior is unspecified: load(N copies of root) yields N TrustAnchors with no dedup
